chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hammad from al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a person in ihram who caught game and gave me some of it, and he said, 'No, it is game of the sanctuary.'
And every game that was slaughtered in the miqat (or open land) is permissible for the one in ihram to eat while in the sanctuary; he narrated that.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically the Haram of Mecca)
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open land / non-sanctuary area (often referring to the miqat or general land outside the Haram boundaries)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game caught by a person in ihram within the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between game caught in the Haram by a muhrim and the permissibility of its consumption based on the recipient's state. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that game caught within the sanctuary remains 'game of the Haram' even if gifted, prohibiting the muhrim from eating it, while game slaughtered in the open land (Hill) is permissible for the muhrim to consume within the Haram. This ruling underscores the spatial sanctity of the Haram boundaries in determining the validity of the sacrifice and consumption rules during Hajj.
